note: Slot 1 (spine b1.3, run-up), revised 10/18 to follow the ch02 choice answered at the door (option 1). The flour at the dawn bell: unmarked, a half-moon of frost glazed from the gap, grains combed toward the door ('breathed in'). Pell came down between all eight bells and sat on the stool set behind Maelis; palms raw. Wren: the seam sweats every dawn she has looked; she starts a page: Times the Captain has asked the Mender (1, then 2). The House wanted the door off its pins; Resolve DC 12 (prof) 18: held to the Mender's count and the Prior's key ('the Mender has my word'), the eager ones sent with Pell's wood. c02.12a fired: Hollis tells Pell to get some sleep, the words he gave the lad. The first day of asking (c02.16a, shape 1): Maelis asks the Prior's question first; 'Come back up.' 'On what?' 'On this.' 'That's the right answer. It isn't true yet. Ask me tomorrow.' (true once Knot III ties: the first stair, slot 4). Ends on Hollis: ask her faster; he's not getting any warmer.
kept_off: What is below; the shard; the satchel; Maelis's past; the Prior's condition.
next_must_know: He asks Maelis each day (Wren counts it). His answer to the Prior's question is 'come back up, on this leg': right, not yet true. The Prior opens the door when he brings her the answer after Maelis's yes. The House is held to the Mender's count and the Prior's key.

note: Between 1 (ch03): the kitchen book has gone even money on NOBODY since the climax ('nobody's hand'); Darrow (candor) refuses to let it be paid out (the bet is no cot grey before the thaw) and turns it into 'Nights without', a stroke per dawn. c02.11a fired: Rae claims the aye: he will tell her what the cold does on the stone, plain, once he has been down (c03.1a, due ch03:s5: on the gate wall the night the House keeps her, before her crate story). The cook's cleaver crossed out as a stake (s1 echo). c02.10b left pending (the book's odds moved; it fires where a cot goes grey or the thaw comes, or the book is next consulted).
next_must_know: Slot 5 owes Rae her aye (c03.1a): he tells her plainly what the cold does on the stone below, before she tells him about the crate. The kitchen keeps a 'Nights without' margin.

note: Between 2 (ch03): Hollis's nightly words to the lad revealed (the truth, one bell at a time: his penance for the kind lie, thread 12/13). Resolve DC 12 (prof) 20: Darrow says the oath aloud for the first time since the river (ch01 between-4 and ch02 s1 were shapes only), for the lad, not the Crown (sworn +1: the old bonds). Hollis watches instead of turning to the wall, and the two of them take the lad's bells in turns, Darrow odd, Hollis even, the fourth Hollis's (c03.2a, a standing colour callback). The oath's words spoken on the page in full (realm.oath; the third line not glossed). Kept off: any response from the lad; nothing of the far cots.
next_must_know: Darrow and Hollis keep the lad's bells in turns at the Grey Cot (Darrow odd, Hollis even, the fourth Hollis's): c03.2a fits any night block at the hall. Darrow has said the oath aloud; Hollis has heard it.

note: Slot 2 (q1.letters compressed, stages 2 and 3), revised 10/19 at his review: the second letter is a real letter in Aldric's voice, guarded because a Confessor carries it ('written for two readers'): Calden says the Ninth broke faith when its captain turned out of the line for one of his own and the Grace left in that moment; Aldric has called it a lie in three rooms and will before the King, given the words; 'I know you. So I know what I am asking.' Then the one unguarded line. The third is a scrap sealed inside, in a faster hand and other ink: answer me, or I will come myself. Darrow's answer to himself: he did turn, and the knee went; but the warmth left first, then the mare, then Tobin, then the turn: Calden tells it backwards, and Aldric on the west bank could not have seen it (thread 1 plant: a question, not a reveal; thread 11 touched). Marrant alone in the fog, courteous; 'a rider of Ser Aldric's' (not 'lord': no rank the page has not given). Dated 'Calden, the third day before the snow': before Coldmere's reading. Hollis sees the blue wax a second time and looks away (T3 plant). Wren: letters three. Micro sworn_unsworn open.
next_must_know: The letters micro is open (default 1, write back as a brother). Tuesday opens with Wren reporting riders on the Holloway under a banner that is not grey (q1.letters stage 3's end). Aldric wrote before the list; 'or I will come myself'.

note: Between 3 (ch03): Darrow asks after the writ (he saw Hollis bring it at the Wend; he has noticed three silences over blue wax). Hollis does not lie to the strong: he has it, never looked at the seal (the hiding place stays off the page: Darrow does not learn it). 'If I look, I'll know whose. And then I'll have to be a man who knows.' Darrow does not ask to see it; asks to be there when he looks: 'Aye. Maybe.' (c03.4a, a later callback for b2.4). c03.2a fired: Hollis says the oath at the even bell, half a breath before 'What I hold I give' (irony unglossed). Darrow writes to Aldric after this (c03.3a, next scene).
next_must_know: Darrow knows Hollis kept the writ and has not looked at the seal; not where it is. c03.4a: Hollis's 'Aye. Maybe.' to Darrow being there when he looks.

threads.who_knows: Hollis knows where his own is and has never looked at its seal; the page has shown him look at a blue seal on Marrant's writ at the bars and watch the blue wax of Darrow's letters (02:s5, 03:s2), saying nothing; Darrow knows (03:between-3) Hollis kept the writ and has never looked at its seal, not where it is; the reader (the leg's cup, 01:interlude)

note: Slot 3 (spine b1.3), revised at his review 10/21. c03.3a paid as the opening: Marrant comes to the bars at the dawn bell to ask for an answer; Darrow hands it unsealed; the letter is given as Marrant reads it ('read by two': Marrant now, Aldric when it reaches him); Marrant's eyes stop once near the middle (which line is left open); 'There's the candour' (callback to 03:s2); he sends it down by one of his men. The letter names Thistle and Tobin (written, not said: 01:s3 'He had not said her name since'; thread 11 'hasn't said his name') and tells Aldric the first letter was burned. c03.3b: Wren counts the letter down with Pell's glass and finds about twenty riders far down the Holloway under a banner not grey, set out before the answer (q1.letters stage 3's end; they do not arrive this chapter). The Knot on the page: for once Maelis does not read the knee at the cot; her count on the nine warming-room steps, her reading at the foot, novices and a lay brother watching (the cost is pride); at five going up he takes his hand off the wall and she puts it back (the turn); 'That's a stair' (callback to 01:s2 'Neither of those is a stair'); her unasked yes: 'Tell the Prior I'll take you down', her count, Wren's shoulder, dusk (c02.16a fired here: the asking was Sun/Mon, the yes unforced). T8 warm: 'as dark down there at noon as at midnight', not as a guess to his ear. The Prior in the chapel: 'Is it true, or only the right thing to say?'; true today; dusk. At dusk the House sups at the kitchen end; Hollis watches from the Grey Cot and calls nothing down; Ione lifts the cord over her head, speaks house.undercroft (the masons built on it, not through) and that no Prior in her line turned the key; turns it two-handed; Wren: keys turned, one; the door sweeps the flour; the cold rises knee-high and the lamp leans from it; Wren first with the lamp, his hand on her shoulder, Maelis behind without a lamp: 'One.' The day's cold colour is shown as his sleeplessness and how he hears Maelis (short), not as cold in his body (Ember Bright in the box).
kept_off: Whose banner the riders carry; Maelis's past below; what is at the bottom; which line stopped Marrant's eye.
next_must_know: Scene 4 (Wed's slot) picks up on the first step down at dusk: Wren first with the lamp, his hand on her shoulder, Maelis behind without a lamp counting from one. Hollis watched from the Grey Cot and called nothing down; slot 4 has him carried to the stair's head to call down 'look at the wall, not the floor' (the lay brothers bring him once they are a few steps down, his voice arriving late). The yes and her terms are already on the page (c02.16a fired). The door is open, the flour swept into a fan; the House is at its supper at the kitchen end. Darrow has not slept since the letters; the riders are far off and not hurrying.

threads.who_knows: Darrow; the reader. Maelis knows only that he believes the Grace was taken, no name. Marrant has read, and Aldric will read, Darrow's order of the ford in his own hand (the warmth first, then Thistle, the boy, the turn) and that he wants to understand 'what I saw from the water'; neither 'ride wide' nor the horse turned early is in it.
threads.note: Darrow has told no one; in Ch 1 Between 2 (revised 10/10) he said aloud to Maelis that the Grace was taken, not lost, and named nobody; she said she does not know whose doing it was. 03:s3: his answer to Aldric gives the order and says he wants to understand 'what I saw from the water' (a question to Aldric, not an accusation); Marrant read it at the gate, his eyes stopping once near the middle.

evaded twice; revised 10/11, Sc 2: she tells him any Confessor who lays a hand on the knee will know what's in it (the danger to her is on the page; her past still is not); the Confessor has looked at her once on the page (b1.2 asks for the Mender by title). 03:s3 (T8 warm): unasked, she says the dark below is the same at noon as at midnight, 'not as a guess' to Darrow's ear; she goes down behind him without a lamp.

threads.who_knows: Darrow; the reader; Marrant (read it) and Aldric (when it reaches him), from Darrow's letter, that he turned toward Tobin. Rae carted his bundle (GM; not on the page).
threads.note: Darrow hasn't said his name aloud; he wrote it in his answer to Aldric (03:s3), with Thistle's.

note: Between 4 (c03.5): on the first step Darrow thanked Wren plainly as a person, not a count; Wren +3, Maelis witnessed. Nothing of the descent itself and nothing below the first step; nothing of her mother (her 'going down and not up' is about this stair only, no plant).
next_must_know: Slot 4 opens on it in a clause: they are still at the Mender's one when he moves; Wren counts him both down and up (c03.5a, color).
